problemStatements.title: TX-LAW-01 · Legal Aid Case Triage and Dynamic Cause-List Scheduling for Odisha's District Courts
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Case Management + Decision Support / Scheduling Optimization + Operations Research

Disciplines: Law, Operations Research, Data Science

Abstract. District courts in Odisha process thousands of cases monthly, but legal aid allocation remains manual and inequitable, leaving indigent litigants unrepresented for extended periods. There is no mechanism to assess urgency, match case complexity to available lawyers, or track aid delivery outcomes systematically. The result is repeated adjournments, prolonged detention, and systemic access gaps particularly for SC/ST and BPL populations.

High-volume courts in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack generate daily cause lists that rarely reflect realistic hearing durations, resulting in courtrooms sitting idle in early hours and severely overloaded by afternoon. Judge and staff time is wasted; litigants and advocates plan their day around unreliable schedules. No data-driven mechanism exists to optimize slot allocation based on case type complexity or historical duration.

Tags. Case triage, Legal aid allocation, Prioritization systems, Court management, Court scheduling, Cause list optimization, Resource efficiency, Duration prediction

problemStatements.title: TX-LAW-02 · Land Mutation Surveillance and Pre-Dispute Alert System for Odisha’s Rural Property Holders
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Real-Time Monitoring + Fraud Detection

Disciplines: Law, GIS, Software Engineering

Abstract. Land mutation fraud and unauthorized record alteration are among the most common sources of civil disputes in rural Odisha, yet registered landowners have no mechanism to be notified when their records are modified in the Bhulekh system. By the time a farmer learns of a fraudulent mutation, costly litigation is already the only recourse. Legal processes for reversal are slow and inaccessible without professional help.

Tags. Land records, Fraud detection, Property rights, Alert systems, Bhulekh

problemStatements.title: TX-LAW-03 · Cyber Threat Intelligence Platform for the Indian Judiciary
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Cybersecurity + Agentic AI

Disciplines: Cybersecurity, Law, Computer Science

Abstract. Judicial databases and e-court portals are prime targets for state-sponsored cyberattacks. Build an agentic cyber-threat-intelligence system that continuously monitors judicial IT infrastructure using honeypots and anomaly detection, auto-classifies attack vectors (ransomware, insider threats, supply-chain attacks), and triggers isolation protocols–while generating legally admissible incident reports that satisfy the IT Act 2000 and DPDPA 2023 breach-notification timelines.

Tags. Threat intelligence, Honeypots, Anomaly detection, Incident response, DPDPA compliance

problemStatements.title: TX-AGR-01 · Autonomous Precision-Spray Coordination System
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Agentic AI + IoT

Disciplines: Engineering, Agriculture, Robotics

Abstract. Individual drone spraying is inefficient at scale. Design a multi-agent drone coordination system where each UAV is an autonomous agent with local perception (multispectral camera + obstacle avoidance), and a central orchestrator allocates tasks, resolves conflicts, and re-plans in response to wind gusts or no-fly micro-zones. The system must guarantee zero-overlap coverage, log spray events immutably, and support over-the-air firmware security patching.

Tags. Drone swarms, Precision spraying, Multi-agent systems, Agricultural IoT, UAV coordination

problemStatements.title: TX-AGR-02 · Pesticide Use Audit and Residue Traceability System for Export-Oriented Horticultural Producers in Odisha
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Supply Chain Traceability + Compliance

Disciplines: Agriculture, Chemistry, Data Science

Abstract. Odisha’s growing vegetable and fruit export sector, particularly ginger, turmeric, and vegetables from Kandhamal and Koraput, faces repeated consignment rejections at export ports due to pesticide residue levels exceeding Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) set by importing countries. Farmers lack real-time guidance on compliant pesticide choices, application timing, and pre-harvest intervals, and there is no digital record of field-level spray activity.

Tags. Pesticide residue, MRL compliance, Export traceability, Spray records, Agri-tech

problemStatements.title: TX-AGR-03 · Intelligent Pump Scheduling and Water Audit Copilot for Odisha’s Lift Irrigation Schemes
problemStatements.description:
Theme: IoT + Resource Optimization

Disciplines: Agriculture, Electrical Engineering, Data Science

Abstract. Odisha operates hundreds of state-owned lift irrigation schemes that are chronically inefficient, pumps run on fixed time schedules regardless of actual soil moisture, crop stage, or weather forecasts, wasting both electricity and water. Scheme operators have no visibility into real-time field conditions, and energy bills routinely exceed department budgets. Unscheduled pump failures during critical crop stages cause significant yield loss.

Tags. Irrigation scheduling, Energy efficiency, Soil moisture sensing, Pump management, Water audit

problemStatements.title: TX-HSM-01 · Surgical Instrument Sterilization Cycle Compliance and Tray Traceability System for Secondary Care Hospitals
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Healthcare Quality + IoT Traceability

Disciplines: Healthcare, Biomedical Engineering, Operations Management

Abstract. Tier-2 hospitals in Odisha lack systematic sterilization cycle tracking for surgical instruments, making it impossible to verify that a given instrument set underwent a validated autoclave cycle before use. Instrument mix-ups between sterile and unprocessed trays occur due to manual handling, with no reliable audit trail. Healthcare-associated infection rates are high, but causation cannot be traced to specific instrument handling lapses.

Tags. Sterilization tracking, Infection control, Instrument traceability, GMP compliance, HAI prevention

problemStatements.title: TX-HSM-02 · ICU Nursing Workload Balancer and Handover Briefing Copilot for Understaffed District Hospitals
problemStatements.description:
Theme: AI-Assisted Clinical Operations

Disciplines: Healthcare, Data Science, Human Factors Engineering

Abstract. ICU nurses in Odisha’s district hospitals routinely manage eight or more critically ill patients per shift due to staffing shortages, creating workload disparities that increase the risk of missed deterioration signs and medication errors. Shift handover briefings are verbal and inconsistent, leading to information loss on patient status changes, pending tasks, and escalation requirements that occurred during the outgoing shift.

Tags. ICU management, Nursing workload, Shift handover, Patient safety, Clinical AI

problemStatements.title: TX-HSM-03 · Patient Discharge Bottleneck Analyzer and Multi-Department Clearance Workflow Automator
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Process Automation + Healthcare Workflow

Disciplines: Healthcare, Operations Management, Software Engineering

Abstract. Patients declared medically ready for discharge in public hospitals frequently remain in wards for three to six additional hours, occupying beds urgently needed by waiting patients, due to sequential delays in billing clearance, pharmacy returns, discharge summary preparation, and transport coordination. These bottlenecks are invisible to administrators because no system captures the time between clinical discharge decision and physical departure.

Tags. Discharge workflow, Bottleneck analysis, Bed management, Multi-dept coordination, Process automation

problemStatements.title: TX-BPH-01 · Herbal Extract Standardization and Regulatory Pathway Guidance Platform for Odisha’s Tribal Medicine Entrepreneurs
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Regulatory Tech + Traditional Medicine

Disciplines: Pharmacy, Biochemistry, Law

Abstract. Odisha’s tribal communities possess documented knowledge of medicinal plant extracts with genuine therapeutic relevance, but commercialization is blocked because producers lack the tools to standardize their preparations, characterize active constituents, and navigate India’s AYUSH licensing and export regulatory pathways. The result is informal sale of unstandardized products with legal and safety risks, forfeiting both IP and market potential.

Tags. Herbal standardization, AYUSH regulation, Traditional medicine, IP protection, Commercialization

problemStatements.title: TX-BPH-02 · Cold Chain Failure Risk Prediction System for Biologic Drug Distribution in Eastern India
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Predictive Analytics + Pharmaceutical Cold Chain

Disciplines: Pharmacy, Supply Chain, Data Science

Abstract. Biologic drugs including insulin, biosimilars, and monoclonal antibodies distributed across eastern India’s pharmaceutical cold chain face significant temperature integrity risks during transit, particularly during summer months when ambient temperatures routinely exceed 42°C in Odisha. Cold chain failures during last-mile distribution are detected only through periodic inspection, often well after product quality is compromised. Patients self-administer biologics without any mechanism to verify whether their medicine has been temperature-compromised.

Tags. Cold chain integrity, Biologics, Temperature risk, Last-mile distribution, Drug quality

problemStatements.title: TX-BPH-03 · AI-Assisted Analysis Platform for Brain Organoid Drug Screening
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Agentic AI + Biomedical Research

Disciplines: Biotechnology, Neuroscience, Computer Vision

Abstract. Brain organoids are revolutionising CNS drug screening, but image analysis is a bottleneck. Build an agentic AI platform that ingests high-content microscopy images of brain organoids, autonomously segments neural structures, quantifies drug-induced morphological changes, integrates electrophysiology data from MEA sensors, and generates structured efficacy/toxicity reports–cutting CNS drug screening timelines from months to days.

Tags. Brain organoids, Drug screening, Image segmentation, Neural morphology, CNS drug discovery

problemStatements.title: TX-ELE-01 · IoT-Based Predictive Health Monitoring for Distribution Transformers
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Predictive Maintenance + IoT

Disciplines: Electrical Engineering, Data Science, Power Systems

Abstract. Distribution transformer failures are the leading cause of rural power outages in Odisha, yet most transformers operate without any monitoring. Install IoT sensors (oil temperature, dissolved gas analysis via DGA, bushing PD, load current) on pole-mounted transformers and build an agentic AI health-monitoring platform that predicts failure 30 days ahead, prioritises maintenance queues by risk, and auto-generates DISCOM work orders.

Tags. Transformer health, Predictive maintenance, IoT sensors, DGA analysis, DISCOM automation

problemStatements.title: TX-ELE-02 · Rooftop Solar Generation Forecast and Grid Injection Variability Management System for Bhubaneswar Urban Clusters
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Renewable Energy + Smart Grid

Disciplines: Electrical Engineering, Data Science, Energy Systems

Abstract. Growing rooftop solar penetration in Bhubaneswar’s residential and commercial areas is introducing significant bidirectional power flows in distribution feeders designed for unidirectional flow, causing voltage regulation challenges. Grid operators currently have no real-time visibility into aggregate rooftop generation within a feeder zone, making demand-supply balancing increasingly difficult during partly-cloudy days when generation swings by 40–60% in minutes.

Tags. Solar forecasting, Grid stability, Voltage regulation, Rooftop solar, DER management

problemStatements.title: TX-ELE-03 · EV Charging Load Coordination System for Residential Apartments and IT Park Campuses
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Smart Grid + EV Infrastructure

Disciplines: Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Data Science

Abstract. Growing EV adoption in Bhubaneswar’s apartment complexes and IT park campuses is creating uncoordinated charging demand spikes, particularly between 6 PM and 10 PM, that push feeder loads beyond capacity limits, causing protective relay trips and damaging transformer equipment. Building electrical infrastructure was not designed for simultaneous multi-EV charging, and no coordination mechanism currently exists to spread load across available charging sessions.

Tags. EV charging, Load management, Demand coordination, Smart charging, Grid protection

problemStatements.title: TX-MEC-01 · Weld Quality Traceability and Process Anomaly Detection System for Coastal Fabrication and Shipbuilding Units
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Quality Traceability + Industrial AI

Disciplines: Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing, Data Science

Abstract. Fabrication yards and ship repair units in coastal Odisha produce structural welds whose quality is verified only through post-completion inspection, discovering defects after rework is expensive and structurally risky. Weld process parameters, heat input, inter-pass temperature, travel speed, are not systematically logged per joint, making defect cause traceability to specific welders, machines, or process conditions impossible. Quality failures at final inspection create costly rework cycles and delivery delays.

Tags. Weld quality, Process traceability, Anomaly detection, Shipbuilding, NDT

problemStatements.title: TX-MEC-02 · Compressed Air Leak Detection and Energy Recovery Advisor for Manufacturing Plants in Odisha
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Energy Efficiency + Industrial IoT

Disciplines: Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Data Science

Abstract. Compressed air systems in manufacturing plants waste 20–30% of compressor input energy through distribution network leaks that are typically undetected until a plant-wide pressure survey is conducted during a planned shutdown. Individual leak points are diffuse, acoustically masked by production noise, and distributed across large pipe networks, making manual ultrasonic detection labor-intensive and infrequent. Energy waste from air leaks is the single largest recoverable loss in most manufacturing plants yet remains consistently unaddressed.

Tags. Compressed air, Leak detection, Energy recovery, Manufacturing efficiency, Acoustic sensing

problemStatements.title: TX-MEC-03 · Cold Storage Refrigeration System Performance Degradation Tracker for Agri-Processing Units in Odisha
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Predictive Maintenance + Food Cold Chain

Disciplines: Mechanical Engineering, Agriculture, Data Science

Abstract. Cold storage facilities serving Odisha’s agri-processing units, handling produce like potato, tomato, and ginger, operate refrigeration systems on fixed compressor schedules without monitoring actual system efficiency, allowing gradual performance degradation from refrigerant leakage, condenser fouling, and compressor valve wear to go undetected until system failure causes a full product loss event. Energy consumption increases silently as efficiency declines, invisible to operators without dedicated monitoring.

Tags. Refrigeration monitoring, Agri cold storage, Compressor health, Degradation tracking, Energy efficiency

problemStatements.title: TX-HLT-01 · Smart Nutrition and Growth Monitoring for Anganwadi and School Children
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Child Health + Digital Health

Disciplines: Nutrition, Public Health, Software Engineering

Abstract. Under-nutrition and anemia remain issues, while manual growth charting and follow-up in Anganwadi centers and schools can be inconsistent.

Tags. Child nutrition, Growth monitoring, Anganwadi, Anemia detection, Digital health

problemStatements.title: TX-HLT-02 · Stray Animal Population Management and Zoonotic Risk Surveillance System for Urban Local Bodies in Odisha
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Urban Health + GIS Analytics

Disciplines: Veterinary Science, Public Health, GIS

Abstract. Urban local bodies in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack manage large populations of stray dogs and urban cattle that pose rabies transmission, road accident, and broader zoonotic disease risks without systematic population data, vaccination coverage maps, or hotspot identification tools. Animal birth control and anti-rabies vaccination programs are conducted without georeferenced population baselines, making coverage assessment impossible and enabling hotspots of under-vaccinated animal populations to persist as outbreak risk zones.

Tags. Stray animals, Rabies surveillance, Animal birth control, Zoonotic risk mapping, Urban health

problemStatements.title: TX-HLT-03 · Post-Surgical Complication Early Detection and Nursing Intervention Guidance System for Surgical Wards
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Clinical AI + Nursing Decision Support

Disciplines: Medicine, Nursing, Data Science

Abstract. Post-operative patients in general surgical wards are monitored through periodic nursing rounds that leave significant time intervals during which early complications, surgical site infection, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and anastomotic leak, develop to symptomatic stages before detection. Nursing staff in high-patient-load Odisha hospitals lack structured complication risk assessment tools, relying on accumulated clinical experience that varies significantly across individual nurses and shifts.

Tags. Post-surgical monitoring, Complication detection, DVT, Surgical site infection, Nursing decision support

problemStatements.title: TX-MGT-01 · Retail Inventory Shrinkage Detection and Loss Attribution System for Grocery and FMCG Chains
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Retail Analytics + Loss Prevention

Disciplines: Management, Retail Operations, Data Science

Abstract. Grocery and FMCG retail chains in Odisha experience inventory shrinkage from theft, spoilage, and mislabeling that cumulatively consumes 2–4% of revenue, yet loss identification is limited to periodic physical stock counts that aggregate losses without attributing them to specific locations, time windows, product categories, or staff shifts. Without attribution granularity, loss prevention efforts cannot be targeted, and the same high-loss conditions persist indefinitely.

Tags. Inventory shrinkage, Loss prevention, Retail analytics, FMCG, Attribution analysis

problemStatements.title: TX-MGT-02 · Integrated Event Operations Management and Real-Time Incident Response System for Large-Scale Institutional Events
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Operations Management + Real-Time Coordination

Disciplines: Management, Event Management, Software Engineering

Abstract. Odisha’s institutional calendar, encompassing university convocations, state sports meets, cultural festivals like Rath Yatra and Mukteshwar Dance Festival, and government summits, involves large-scale event operations managed through fragmented WhatsApp groups, paper checklists, and verbal coordination that create information gaps, delayed incident response, and post-event accountability failure. No unified operations platform exists that coordinates venue setup, crowd management, vendor delivery, and emergency response in real time.

Tags. Event management, Incident response, Real-time coordination, Crowd management, Smart city ops

problemStatements.title: TX-MGT-03 · Municipal Grievance SLA Breach Predictor and Proactive Escalation System for Bhubaneswar Smart City Corporation
problemStatements.description:
Theme: Civic Tech + Predictive Analytics

Disciplines: Public Administration, Data Science, Software Engineering

Abstract. Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation’s citizen grievance portal receives thousands of complaints monthly, covering roads, drainage, sanitation, water supply, and street lighting, but response times routinely exceed statutory SLA windows due to manual routing, absence of priority weighting, and no mechanism for proactive escalation when a ticket is trending toward breach. Repeat complaints on the same issue and delayed resolution erode citizen trust and create public accountability gaps.

Tags. Grievance management, SLA prediction, Smart city, Citizen services, Proactive escalation
